title: When a Permitted Action Completes a Forbidden Workflow: Designing Consequence-Oriented Approval for LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.28454v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Tool-using language-model agents increasingly ask people to approve consequential actions, yet an approval prompt shows only the next step. A request to send a file to an approved recipient can look harmless even when that file was assembled, several steps earlier, from data the user said must never leave. We call this a cumulative authorization failure and argue that it is an interaction design problem as much as a security problem. The evidence a reviewer needs is spread across the trajectory, and listing it in time order leaves the reviewer to reconstruct the causal chain. We present the Cumulative Consent Ledger (CCL), an approval interface built on four design principles that restate the user's intent, bind the review to the exact action, compose the cumulative consequence, and keep every claim checkable. translated_title: 当一个被允许的操作完成了被禁止的工作流：为LLM智能体设计面向后果的审批机制
translated_abstract: 使用工具的语言模型智能体越来越多地要求人们批准具有重大影响的操作，然而审批提示只显示下一步操作。一个向已获批准接收者发送文件的请求可能看起来无害，即使该文件早在几个步骤之前，就是由用户声明绝不能外传的数据组装而成的。我们将这种现象称为累积性授权失败，并认为它既是安全问题，也是交互设计问题。审阅者所需的证据分散在整个轨迹中，按时间顺序罗列这些证据会让审阅者不得不自行重建因果链。我们提出了累积同意账本，这是一个基于四项设计原则构建的审批界面：重述用户意图、将审查绑定到具体操作、合成累积后果，以及保持每项声明可验证。一个追踪工件来源的可信监视器负责提供证据。在一项包含80名参与者和960个实验样本的被试间实验中（原文截断）……
tldr: 该论文提出累积同意账本（CCL）这一审批界面，通过重述用户意图、绑定具体操作、合成累积后果、保持声明可验证四项设计原则，解决LLM智能体中单个被允许的操作累积完成被禁止工作流的授权失败问题。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes the Cumulative Consent Ledger (CCL), an approval interface built on four design principles—restating user intent, binding review to the exact action, composing cumulative consequences, and keeping claims checkable—to address cumulative authorization failures where individually permitted actions combine to complete a forbidden workflow in LLM agents.
